story.originalTitle: Wolff: Russell-Verstappen provocations a good factor of F1 entertainment
story.summaryEn: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says the "provocations" between his driver George Russell and Red Bull's Max Verstappen are a "good factor of the entertainment" in Formula 1.
detailZh: 梅赛德斯领队托托·沃尔夫表示，马克斯·维斯塔潘与乔治·拉塞尔的竞争是F1娱乐性的“好因素”。
马克斯·维斯塔潘与乔治·拉塞尔之间长期的不和在拉斯维加斯大奖赛上再度激化；拉塞尔在第三次练习赛中两人发生碰撞后批评了维斯塔潘；维斯塔潘在赢得分站冠军后嘲讽了退赛的拉塞尔。
马克斯·维斯塔潘在赢下拉斯维加斯大奖赛后，对老对手乔治·拉塞尔说了几句简短的话。
梅赛德斯领队托托·沃尔夫表示，旗下车手乔治·拉塞尔与红牛车手马克斯·维斯塔潘之间的“挑衅”是F1娱乐性的“好因素”。
两人之间的敌对情绪在拉斯维加斯大奖赛上再度燃起，最后一次练习赛中的碰撞之后，双方又爆发了一场口水战，这场口水战有可能在下周末的卡塔尔大奖赛上继续上演，天空体育F1频道将从周五开始直播。
在周六晚上的拉斯维加斯正赛之前，拉塞尔曾批评过维斯塔潘，随后两人在比赛中为领先位置展开了长时间的争夺，维斯塔潘最终夺冠，而拉塞尔在比赛后段出现失误——当时他试图超越队友安东内利升至第二——名次大幅下滑，最终以第九名完赛。
“他远低于我的水平”——马克斯·维斯塔潘嘲讽乔治·拉塞尔的失误

维斯塔潘当时在车队无线电中调侃了拉塞尔，随后在赛后新闻发布会上又抨击了这位梅赛德斯车手，声称“他远低于我的水平”。
在拉斯维加斯大奖赛上，乔治·拉塞尔在试图超越队友基米·安东内利时锁死轮胎撞上护栏，这让对手马克斯·维斯塔潘大为高兴。
沃尔夫在赛后、维斯塔潘出席新闻发布会之前发言，暗示这种竞争对这项运动有好处。
当被问及拉塞尔对维斯塔潘玩“心理战”是否是个坏主意时，沃尔夫回答说：“他们从卡丁车时代就认识彼此这么久了。”
“我觉得这大概有点像猫捉老鼠的游戏。”
乔治·拉塞尔对拉斯维加斯大奖赛最后一次练习中与马克斯·维斯塔潘的碰撞做出了回应，指责这位红牛车手“坑害”了他的对手。
“双方之间的这些挑衅也是娱乐性的另一个好因素。”
他们的恩怨几乎正好在两年后再次点燃，此前2024年卡塔尔大奖赛后曾爆发重大冲突，当时维斯塔潘认为拉塞尔为让干事处罚自己而施压过度，随后引发了一场引人注目的口水战。
2026年拉斯维加斯大奖赛精彩集锦
两人在最后一次练习中的碰撞发生在维斯塔潘超越拉塞尔之后，当时两人都在为飞驰圈做准备，拉塞尔认为这违反了车手之间的一项君子协定。
干事因造成碰撞而向维斯塔潘发出警告，拉塞尔接受这一结果并认为处理得当，但他坚持表示“总得有人站出来对抗那家伙”。
当被问及是否知道两人在事件发生后是否有过交谈时，沃尔夫表示：“我猜在赛事干事室里有一些交流。”
乔治·拉塞尔在拉斯维加斯大奖赛起步时与马克斯·维斯塔潘和伊萨克·哈贾尔缠斗
维斯塔潘驾驶出色赢得比赛，他精准地管理能量部署，多次立即夺回领先位置。
在刘易斯·汉密尔顿确认离开梅赛德斯加盟法拉利后，沃尔夫曾公开向维斯塔潘示好，他对这位荷兰人的表现印象深刻。
"我认为马克斯是一位当之无愧的（比赛）获胜者。他没有犯任何错误，这就是他赢得比赛的原因。
"他总是能做出回应。一些非常出色的驾驶。"

detailEn: Max Verstappen rivalry with George Russell 'a good factor' of F1 entertainment, says Mercedes chief Toto Wolff

A long-standing feud between Max Verstappen and George Russell was reignited at the Las Vegas Grand Prix; Russell criticised Verstappen following a collision between the pair in final practice; Verstappen taunted Russell after winning the race as the Mercedes driver crashed out
Max Verstappen had a choice few words for long-time foe George Russell after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff says the "provocations" between his driver George Russell and Red Bull's Max Verstappen are a "good factor of the entertainment" in Formula 1.

Hostilities between the pair were renewed at the Las Vegas Grand Prix as a collision in final practice was followed by a war of words that threatens to continue at next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday.

After Russell had criticised Verstappen ahead of Saturday night's race in Las Vegas, the pair battled for the lead for much of the race, with Verstappen claiming victory as Russell finished ninth after a late error - made as he tried to pass his team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second - dropped the Brit down the field.
'He's so far below my level' - Max Verstappen taunts George Russell over error

Verstappen poked fun at Russell at the time over team radio and then laid into the Mercedes driver during the post-race press conference, claiming that "he's so far below my level".
George Russell hits the barrier after a lock-up when trying to overtake team-mate Kimi Antonelli at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, much to the delight of rival Max Verstappen
Wolff, who was speaking after the race but before Verstappen had spoken in the press conference, suggested the rivalry was good for the sport.
Asked whether it was a bad idea for Russell to engage in 'mind games' with Verstappen, Wolff replied: "They have known each other so long since karting.
"I think it's probably been a bit of cat and mouse.
George Russell reacted to the collision with Max Verstappen in final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, accusing the Red Bull driver of of 'screwing' his rivals over
"These provocations in either side is another good factor of the entertainment."

Their feud has reignited almost exactly two years on from a major blow up following the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, which saw a remarkable war of words follow an incident in which Verstappen felt Russell had pushed unreasonably hard to get him penalised by the stewards.
Highlights from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix

The collision between the pair in final practice happened after Verstappen had overtaken Russell as the pair were both preparing for push laps, which Russell felt was in breach of a gentleman's agreement the drivers have.
The stewards gave Verstappen a warning for causing the collision, which Russell accepted as an appropriate outcome, but he insisted that "somebody's got to stand up to that guy".
Asked if he knew whether the pair had exchanged words following the incident, Wolff said: "I guess in the stewards' room there was a bit of an exchange."
George Russell tussles with Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar at the start of the Las Vegas Grand Prix
Verstappen drove superbly to win the race, managing his deployment expertly to immediately regain the lead on several occasions.
Wolff, who publicly courted Verstappen after it was confirmed Lewis Hamilton was leaving Mercedes to join Ferrari, was impressed by the Dutchman's display.
"I think Max is a deserving winner [of the race]. He made no mistakes, and that's why he won the race.
"He always had a response. Some very good driving."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
